title: Channel runner foundation: validate inputs before calculation
value: A focused first work packet for the outstanding custom-channel runner: reject malformed channel inputs and invalid solver settings before any numerical calculation.
why_now: Catch-up entry requested and written on November 12 for the missed 2026-11-10 review. This develops a bounded part of the channel-runner proposal that was already outstanding on November 9; it does not assert that a review or implementation occurred on the missed date. The evidence was inspected on November 12, including the documented input assumptions and iteration-limit caveat. Both work packets are proposals, with reporting dependent on validation. The current November 12 backup-transport recommendation remains the latest priority; these retrospective entries do not replace it. No numerical solver or scheduler tests were executed for this retrospective source review.
effort: About 1-2 hours for a shared validator and focused tests
steps: Add a shared validation helper or wrapper for a nonempty rectangular 2-D numeric matrix with finite, nonnegative entries and row sums within an explicitly documented tolerance of one.

Validate solver settings: finite positive tolerance and a positive integer iteration limit; document the supported relaxed-mode parameter range instead of implying every alpha accelerates convergence.
Return concise actionable errors; do not silently normalize invalid probabilities or alter the original research solver behavior.
Cover malformed matrices, legitimate zero probabilities, and accepted BSC/asymmetric examples with regression tests, then run the existing numerical suite.
acceptance_checks: Empty, ragged, nonnumeric, negative, nonfinite and nonnormalized matrices are rejected clearly.
Valid stochastic matrices including zero probabilities pass unchanged within the documented row-sum tolerance.
Zero or nonfinite tolerance and zero, negative or noninteger iteration limits fail before invoking the solver.
Existing analytic capacity tests remain passing; no acceleration or implementation completion is claimed by this plan.

evidence.observation: Source inspected on November 12: the solver converts and unpacks the matrix without explicit validation, returns the final bound gap and iteration count, and can update p after the last evaluated bounds.
Documentation inspected on November 12 states valid-matrix assumptions, capacity in bits, tolerance in nats, and the iteration-limit consistency caveat.
Entry point inspected on November 12 hardcodes Processes.txt and calls generate_gantt_chart after calculating metrics. A configurable headless runner is an alternative usability task.
Source inspected on November 12 contains an explicitly marked network_send_all stub that ignores its arguments and returns success; this supports the current November 12 priority.
